observation.visible_scene: A low-angle view of a forest stream cascading over dark, wet rocks. A mossy green bank lines the left side, a large tree trunk and an arching leafy branch frame the right and top, and a bright misty haze fills the center background where the waterway recedes. The composition and framing of the trees, branch, and rocks remain identical from the first to the last frame, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The whitewater and foam on the stream surface continuously reshape and shift between frames, consistent with water flowing toward the viewer over the rocks; no single wave or foam patch persists unchanged.
The texture of the rushing water in the foreground and midground churns and re-forms throughout the excerpt, while the dark wet rocks beneath it stay fixed in place.
The misty glow in the background remains broadly steady, with only faint, indeterminate variation in its soft edges.
outside_clip_unknowns: The upstream source and downstream continuation of the stream, and the cause of the mist, lie outside this segment.
Whether the water flow speeds up, slows, or stops after the last frame is not shown.
Any camera movement before the first frame or after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the canopy leaves sway slightly or are motionless cannot be confirmed at this resolution.
Whether the background haze drifts or is a static volumetric glow is not clearly resolvable.
The exact direction and speed of the water flow are inferred from changing foam patterns rather than tracked individual parcels.
